story: Late one night old Mrs. Peabody is walking home alone. She doesn't like walking home alone in the dark because she is always afraid that someone will jump out at her and rob her. She really is a very nervous person. Suddenly, out of the shadows comes a man. He wants to ask Mrs. Peabody what time it is, so he walks toward her. When Mrs. Peabody sees the man coming toward her, she starts to tremble and says, 'Take my purse, just don't hurt me, please!'
question: Why did Mrs. Peabody say that?
correct_answer: She mistakenly thought the man was going to rob her, even though he only wanted to ask the time.
distractor_answer: She wanted to give the man her purse as a gift.

story: Today James is going to Claire's house for the first time. He is going there for tea, and he is looking forward to seeing Claire's dog, which she talks about all the time. James likes dogs very much. When James arrives at Claire's house, Claire opens the door. Behind her stands a huge dog, almost as big as James! James says, 'Claire, I love your dog!'
question: Is it true what James said?
correct_answer: Not quite. James is being polite or perhaps scared, but his comment is meant kindly even if not literally true.
distractor_answer: Yes, he loves all big dogs.

story: A burglar who has just robbed a shop is making his way home. As he walks home, a policeman on his beat sees him drop his glove. He doesn't know the man is a burglar; he just wants to tell him he dropped his glove. But when the policeman shouts out to the burglar, 'Hey, you! Stop!' the burglar turns round, sees the policeman and gives himself up. He puts his hands up and admits that he did the break-in at the local shop.
question: Why did the burglar do that when the policeman didn't actually know he had robbed the shop?
correct_answer: The burglar misinterpreted the policeman's words as a confrontation about the robbery; he didn't realize the policeman was only trying to return his glove.
distractor_answer: The burglar was a kind man who wanted to thank the policeman.

story: Brian is always hungry. Today at school it is his favorite meal: sausages and beans. He is a very greedy boy and he would like to have more sausages than anybody else, even though his mother will have made him a lovely meal at home, too. But everyone is allowed two sausages and no more. When it is Brian's turn to be served, he says, 'Oh, please can I have four sausages, because I won't be having any dinner when I get home!'
question: Why does Brian say this?
correct_answer: He is lying about not having dinner at home so that he can get more sausages than the other children.
distractor_answer: He actually wasn't going to have dinner at home that day.

story: Helen waited all year for Christmas, because she knew at Christmas she could ask her parents for a rabbit. Helen wanted a rabbit more than anything in the world. At last Christmas Day arrived, and Helen ran to unwrap the big box her parents had given her. She felt sure it would contain a little rabbit in a cage. But when she opened it, with all the family standing round, she found her present was just a boring old set of encyclopedias, which Helen did not want at all! Still, when Helen's parents asked her how she liked her Christmas present, she said, 'It's lovely, thank you. It's just what I wanted.'
question: Why did Helen say that?
correct_answer: She told a white lie to spare her parents' feelings and not seem ungrateful.
distractor_answer: She had changed her mind and now wanted encyclopedias.

story: During the war, the Red Army captured a member of the Blue Army. They wanted to know where the Blue Army's tanks were hidden. They knew the tanks were either in the mountains or in the sea. They knew the prisoner would not want to reveal the location, but they also knew he would try to lie. The prisoner is very brave. When the Red Army asks him where the tanks are, he says, 'They are in the mountains.'
question: Why did the prisoner say that, given that the tanks really were in the mountains?
correct_answer: He told the truth expecting the Red Army to assume he was lying, so they would search the sea and not find the tanks.
distractor_answer: He was confused about where the tanks were located.

story: Simon is a big liar. Simon's brother Jim knows this; he knows that Simon never tells the truth! Now yesterday Simon stole Jim's ping-pong paddle, and Jim knows Simon has hidden it somewhere, though he can't find it. He's very cross. So he finds Simon and he says, 'Where is my ping-pong paddle? You must have hidden it either in the cupboard or under your bed, because I've looked everywhere else. Where is it, in the cupboard or under your bed?' Simon tells him the paddle is under his bed.
question: Why will Jim look in the cupboard for the paddle?
correct_answer: Because Jim knows Simon is a liar, so when Simon says 'under the bed,' Jim will assume the truth is the opposite and look in the cupboard.
distractor_answer: Because the cupboard is closer to where Jim is standing.

story: One day Aunt Jane came to visit Peter. Now Peter loves his aunt very much, but today she is wearing a new hat; a new hat which Peter thinks is very ugly indeed. Peter thinks his aunt looks silly in it, and much nicer in her old hat. But when Aunt Jane asks Peter, 'How do you like my new hat?', Peter says, 'Oh, it's very nice.'
question: Why does Peter say that?
correct_answer: Peter is being polite and telling a white lie so as not to hurt his aunt's feelings.
distractor_answer: Peter actually thinks the hat looks nice.

story: Late one night, Mr. Brown is on his way to bed when he hears a noise downstairs. He goes down to investigate and finds that his television and stereo have been stolen. He notices a window has been forced open. The next day, when the police come, Mr. Brown says, 'I'm just glad they didn't take the cat too!'
question: Why did Mr. Brown say that?
correct_answer: He was making a joke to lighten the mood about a stressful situation.
distractor_answer: He genuinely worried that the cat had been stolen.

story: Sarah and Tom are going on a picnic. It is Tom's idea, he says it is going to be a lovely sunny day for a picnic. But just as they are unpacking the food, it starts to rain, and soon they are both soaked to the skin. Sarah is cross. She says, 'Oh yes, what a lovely day for a picnic alright!'
question: Why does Sarah say that?
correct_answer: Sarah is being sarcastic; she means the opposite of what she says, complaining about the bad weather Tom predicted would be good.
distractor_answer: Sarah genuinely thinks the rainy day is lovely.

story: Jill wanted to buy a kitten, so she went to see Mrs. Smith who had lots of kittens she didn't want. Mrs. Smith loved the kittens, and she wouldn't do anything to harm them, though she couldn't keep them all herself. When Jill visited she wasn't sure she wanted one of Mrs. Smith's kittens, since they were all males and she had wanted a female. But Mrs. Smith said, 'If no one buys the kittens I'll just have to drown them!'
question: Why did Mrs. Smith say that?
correct_answer: She said it to persuade Jill to take a kitten by making her feel sorry for them, even though she would never actually harm them.
distractor_answer: She really intended to drown the kittens that day.

story: Mike, a nine-year-old boy, often forgets to brush his teeth. One day his Mum says to him, 'Now Mike, do you brush your teeth twice a day?' Mike says, 'Oh yes, of course I do!' In fact he hasn't brushed his teeth for two days.
question: Why did Mike say what he said?
correct_answer: Mike lied to his mother so he wouldn't get in trouble for not brushing his teeth.
distractor_answer: Mike forgot what brushing teeth means.

story: Sarah is bored. She has nothing to do. She picks up a banana and puts it to her ear like a telephone. She says, 'Hello, who's there?'
question: Why does Sarah put the banana to her ear?
correct_answer: She is pretending the banana is a telephone, playing a game of make-believe.
distractor_answer: She thinks the banana is actually a phone.

story: Daniel and Jessica's grandfather was very ill in the hospital. He was not expected to live much longer. Yesterday, the family received the sad news that Grandfather had passed away. When Jessica is told the news, she bursts into tears. Daniel says to his mother, 'I'm not going to cry. Grandpa wouldn't want us to.'
question: Why did Daniel say that?
correct_answer: Daniel is hiding his sadness or trying to be brave; he likely feels grief but is trying to manage it.
distractor_answer: Daniel did not feel sad about grandfather's death.

story: Anna's mother had spent a long time making Anna's favorite meal: fish and chips. But when she brought it in to Anna, she was watching TV, and she didn't even look up, or say thank you. Anna's mother was cross. She said, 'Well, that's very nice, isn't it! That's what I call politeness!'
question: Why did Anna's mother say that?
correct_answer: Anna's mother was being sarcastic; she meant the opposite, that Anna was being impolite.
distractor_answer: Anna's mother thought Anna was being very polite.

story: Two boys, Tom and Sam, are walking past a bakery. Tom says, 'Mm, that bread smells wonderful, I'm so hungry I could eat a horse!'
question: Is it true what Tom said?
correct_answer: Not literally; he means he is very hungry. It is a figure of speech.
distractor_answer: Yes, he literally could eat a horse.

story: Late one night, a man is walking past a cemetery. He hears a tapping sound. Frightened, he stops to investigate, and he finds an old man tapping a chisel on a gravestone. The old man explains, 'They spelled my name wrong on this gravestone.'
question: Why does the old man say his name is spelled wrong on the gravestone?
correct_answer: The old man is making a joke, since people don't usually carve their own gravestones.
distractor_answer: He is actually a stonemason who chose to work at night.

story: Emma's class went on a school trip to the zoo. Emma's favorite animal at the zoo was the elephant. When she came home, her brother asked her, 'How big was the elephant?' Emma said, 'Oh, the elephant was as big as a mountain!'
question: Is it true that the elephant was as big as a mountain?
correct_answer: No, Emma is using hyperbole. She means the elephant was very large but not literally as big as a mountain.
distractor_answer: Yes, the zoo had a mountain-sized elephant.

story: Mark and his sister Lucy are playing tag in the backyard. After a few minutes of chasing, Lucy collapses dramatically on the lawn and lies still with her eyes closed. Mark comes over and pretends to check her pulse with a serious face. Lucy then opens one eye and giggles.
question: Why did Lucy lie down with her eyes closed?
correct_answer: She was pretending to be dead or hurt as part of a game.
distractor_answer: She actually fainted from running.

story: Sam was making a sandwich. He took out the bread, opened the jar of peanut butter, and started spreading it. But he was thinking about his upcoming test, and accidentally he put the peanut butter on the bread in a sandwich shape with the slices in the wrong order. His brother walked in, saw the sandwich, and laughed. Sam asked his brother, 'What are you laughing at?' His brother said, 'You've made a peanut butter sandwich on the outside instead of the inside.'
question: Why did Sam make the sandwich wrong?
correct_answer: Sam was distracted thinking about his test and didn't pay attention to what he was doing.
distractor_answer: Sam was trying to invent a new kind of sandwich on purpose.

story: A little boy named Kevin has just learned about the planets in school. He runs home and tells his mother, 'Mom! I'm going to walk to Pluto tomorrow!' His mother smiles and says, 'That sounds like a great plan, sweetheart.'
question: Why did Kevin's mother respond that way?
correct_answer: She didn't want to discourage his enthusiasm or curiosity; she went along with his imagination.
distractor_answer: She actually believes Kevin can walk to Pluto.

story: Two old friends, John and Bill, hadn't seen each other in twenty years. They met by chance in a cafe. John said, 'Bill, my old friend! I would have recognized you anywhere; you haven't changed a bit!' In truth, Bill had aged considerably and looked very different.
question: Why did John say that?
correct_answer: John was being polite or kind; he said something not literally true to make Bill feel good.
distractor_answer: Bill really hasn't aged at all in twenty years.

story: Susan is a champion runner. She won her last race in record time. Today she has another race. As she lines up at the starting line, her teammate says, 'Now don't go and lose this one.'
question: What does the teammate mean?
correct_answer: The teammate is teasing Susan because they know she is very likely to win again; it is friendly sarcasm.
distractor_answer: The teammate genuinely worries Susan will lose.

story: Linda's dog had to go to the vet for an operation. The next day, Linda told her young son, 'Don't worry, the dog is just away on a special vacation, but he'll be fine.' In truth, the dog had died on the operating table.
question: Why did Linda say that?
correct_answer: Linda lied to protect her young son from the painful truth that the dog had died.
distractor_answer: Linda was confused about what happened to the dog.

story: Henry, a clumsy boy, slipped and fell flat on his face while walking through the cafeteria. The whole cafeteria saw it. As he got up, his friend Greg called out, 'Smooth move, Henry!'
question: What does Greg mean?
correct_answer: Greg is being sarcastic; he means the opposite of smooth, teasing Henry about his fall.
distractor_answer: Greg genuinely thinks Henry's fall was smooth.

story: A poor man went to a wealthy neighbor asking to borrow money for his sick child's medicine. The wealthy man refused. Later that day, the wealthy man's dog ran away. The poor man, walking by, saw the dog and brought it back to the wealthy man. The wealthy man tried to give him a reward. The poor man said, 'No thank you. I help out of kindness, not for money.'
question: Why did the poor man refuse the reward?
correct_answer: The poor man wanted to teach the wealthy man a lesson about kindness and act with dignity even after being refused help himself.
distractor_answer: The poor man did not need the money anymore.

story: Eight-year-old Maggie wanted a pony for her birthday more than anything in the world. On her birthday, her parents gave her a stuffed pony instead of a real one. Maggie smiled and said, 'Thank you, it's perfect.' Later that night, her mother heard her crying in her room.
question: Why did Maggie smile and say thank you?
correct_answer: Maggie hid her disappointment because she didn't want to hurt her parents' feelings, but she really wanted a real pony.
distractor_answer: Maggie was happy with the stuffed pony.

story: A new student joined Mark's class. Mark wanted to make him feel welcome. He went up to the new student at lunch and said, 'There's an empty seat at our table. Come sit with us.'
question: Why did Mark say that?
correct_answer: Mark wanted to make the new student feel welcome and included.
distractor_answer: Mark wanted to give up his seat at the table.

story: Two children, Anna and Mia, are playing a game where they pretend to be doctors. Anna takes a wooden block and holds it up to Mia's chest. Anna says, 'Your heart sounds fine.'
question: What is Anna doing?
correct_answer: Anna is pretending the wooden block is a stethoscope as part of the game.
distractor_answer: Anna actually believes the wooden block can hear heartbeats.

story: Sandra had spent hours preparing a meal for her boyfriend's parents, but the chicken came out burnt and dry. When she served it, the parents took small bites and said, 'This is delicious, thank you.'
question: Why did the parents say that?
correct_answer: The parents were being polite and didn't want to hurt Sandra's feelings after she'd worked so hard.
distractor_answer: The parents really love burnt and dry chicken.

story: Two thieves planned to rob a bank. They knew the police were watching them. Thief A says to Thief B in a public place, where they suspect police are listening, 'We'll do the bank job on Tuesday at noon.' In fact, they had planned to do it on Wednesday at midnight.
question: Why did Thief A say that?
correct_answer: Thief A was deliberately misleading the police, who were listening in, so the police would prepare for the wrong day and time.
distractor_answer: Thief A actually forgot the real plan.

story: Anna was nervous about giving her first big presentation at work. She had practiced for weeks. After she gave the talk, her boss said, 'You really hit it out of the park, Anna!'
question: What does her boss mean?
correct_answer: It is a baseball metaphor; the boss means Anna did an excellent job.
distractor_answer: Anna literally hit a baseball during her presentation.

story: Tom and Jerry are playing a game. Tom takes a stick and pretends it is a sword. He waves it around and says, 'I am a brave knight!' Jerry runs and grabs a pot to put on his head. He says, 'And I am a knight too!'
question: What are Tom and Jerry doing?
correct_answer: They are playing make-believe, pretending to be knights using everyday objects as their equipment.
distractor_answer: They actually believe they are knights now.

story: Lisa knew her sister Carol was secretly afraid of spiders. One April Fools' Day, Lisa put a rubber spider in Carol's bed. When Carol pulled back the covers, she screamed and jumped. Lisa burst out laughing. Carol said, 'Lisa, that wasn't funny!'
question: What was Lisa trying to do?
correct_answer: Lisa was playing an April Fools' prank, trying to scare and tease her sister as a joke.
distractor_answer: Lisa actually wanted to harm Carol.

story: Marie left her car at the auto shop because the engine was making noise. The mechanic told her it would cost $200. When she came back, the bill was $400. The mechanic explained he found additional problems. Marie suspected he was overcharging her. She said calmly, 'Oh wonderful, what a great surprise.'
question: What does Marie mean?
correct_answer: She is being sarcastic; she means it is not a wonderful surprise at all, and she is upset about the extra charge.
distractor_answer: She is genuinely happy about the extra charge.

story: Ben's grandfather had been very sick for months. When Ben visited him in the hospital, his grandfather smiled weakly and said, 'I'm doing great. Don't worry about me.' Ben looked at the tubes and machines around him and saw the tired look in his grandfather's eyes.
question: Was the grandfather telling Ben the truth?
correct_answer: No, the grandfather was lying kindly to spare Ben worry; he was clearly not doing great.
distractor_answer: Yes, the grandfather felt completely fine.

story: Tony saw his friend Carl at the grocery store. Carl was sneaking a chocolate bar into his pocket without paying. Tony pretended he hadn't seen and walked the other way. Later, Tony confronted Carl privately and said, 'I saw what you did.' Carl looked embarrassed and said, 'I didn't want to lose your friendship.'
question: Why did Tony confront Carl privately rather than at the store?
correct_answer: Tony wanted to address Carl's behavior without publicly embarrassing him or getting him arrested.
distractor_answer: Tony wanted to steal something too without being caught.

story: Five-year-old Lila was upset because her parents wouldn't let her have ice cream before dinner. She stomped to her room and slammed the door. A minute later she yelled, 'I'm not coming out ever again!'
question: Did Lila really mean she would never come out?
correct_answer: No, she was exaggerating to express her anger and frustration in the moment.
distractor_answer: Yes, Lila plans to stay in her room forever.

story: Ethan was applying for a competitive scholarship. He had to write an essay. When he finished, his friend Rachel read it. She thought it was full of grammar mistakes and weak arguments. But she said, 'It's really thoughtful. I'm sure the committee will appreciate it.'
question: Why did Rachel say that?
correct_answer: Rachel didn't want to discourage Ethan or hurt his confidence, so she gave a kind but not fully honest response.
distractor_answer: Rachel genuinely thought the essay was excellent.

story: A magician at a children's party pulled a rabbit out of a hat. The young children gasped and clapped. A nine-year-old boy named Sam called out, 'I know how you did it! The rabbit was hidden in a secret compartment!' The magician smiled and continued without confirming.
question: Why did the magician not confirm Sam's explanation?
correct_answer: The magician wanted to preserve the magic and wonder for the other children who still believed in the trick.
distractor_answer: The magician did not understand what Sam said.
